name: Narrative Structure
description: Examines the pacing, act division, and temporal flow of a text. AI models tend to produce highly symmetric, predictable, and 'flat' narrative arcs, often resolving conflicts too quickly or structuring stories into mathematically even sections (e.g., rigid five-paragraph essays or perfectly balanced three-act stories) without organic pacing.
algorithm: Temporal Discourse Analysis and Arc Symmetry Detection
mechanism: This algorithm segments the text and maps its narrative trajectory by analyzing discourse markers, temporal shifts (e.g., 'Later that day', 'Meanwhile'), and the distribution of conflict/resolution keywords. Large Language Models (LLMs) optimize for structural completeness and safety within a limited context window. When asked to write a story or an essay, they instinctively default to a highly standardized, boilerplate template: a brief introduction, equally weighted body paragraphs/events, and a neat, unambiguous conclusion. They struggle to create 'messy', organic pacing, anti-climaxes, or structurally asymmetrical narratives (like spending 80% of a text on the build-up and 20% on a sudden resolution). Human writers naturally vary their pacing; they might linger on a specific descriptive tangent, utilize flashbacks, or abruptly shift narrative speed. The system calculates a 'Narrative Symmetry Score'. A score that is too perfect—where introduction, rising action, climax, and resolution occur at mathematically predictable word-count milestones—strongly flags the text as procedurally generated by an AI adhering to its training templates.
useCase: Crucial for evaluating creative writing, student essays, and marketing copy, identifying content that feels rigidly formulaic, 'too perfect', or lacking the organic flow characteristic of human thought.
strengths:
• Highly effective against 'zero-shot' AI generations where the user simply asks the model to 'write an essay about X' without providing a specific, chaotic structural outline.
• Detects the underlying structural bias of the model, which remains intact even if individual words are spun or replaced by a human.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives when analyzing highly structured human writing, such as strict five-paragraph academic essays, standardized corporate reports, or news articles adhering strictly to the 'inverted pyramid' style.
• Cannot effectively analyze very short texts (under 300 words) where a full narrative arc is impossible to establish.
• Deeply engineered prompts that instruct the AI to mimic avant-garde or non-linear structures can bypass this metric.
parameters:
Analysis: Discourse Segmentation and Temporal Marker Distribution
Metric: Arc Symmetry and Pacing Variance
Output: 0-100 Structural Rigidity (Formulaic Predictability) Score
accuracy: Moderate — 65-75% accuracy. It is an excellent secondary metric for detecting 'lazy' prompting, but requires context regarding the expected genre structure to avoid penalizing intentionally formulaic human writing.

references.title: Jurafsky, D. & Martin, J.H. (2024). Speech and Language Processing. 3rd Edition.
Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
